research_concepts: play-type possession labels derived from play-by-play
unit-level consistency across teams or matchups
methodological_questions: Does a PNR-fail-then-PULL_UP sequence show positive lift over a matched baseline in at least 70% of units, with median lift above 2pp?
What unit definition, minimum sample size and baseline are needed to estimate counter lift reliably?
Are the PNR-fail and PULL_UP labels valid, and are they free of outcome-derived or assisted-flag artifacts?

historical_evidence.finding: Observed on-ball coverage labels (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup/PBP fields were labelled on only 14.9% (DET, 10 of 67 possessions) and 3.3% (ORL, 2 of 60) of possessions; switches_on was not populated. Verdict: failed_gate.

A play-type classifier using the assisted flag, which exists only on makes, produced SPOT_UP 2.83 PPP with 100% makes. After rewriting, SPOT_UP was about 1.16 and TRANSITION about 1.20. The record is an engineering discovery that poisoned a simulation.

Holdout validation of pre-game play-type PPP ranking on 908 game-team rows from 454 games: median rho +0.539; 88.4% rho>0; 10.5% rho<0; median top-3 lift +0.4261 PPP. The record notes the top-3 lift partly reflects league-wide high-efficiency play types (CUT, PUTBACK, TRANSITION). This concerns play-type efficiency ranking, not counter lift.

Opponent-relative leverage sweep over 870 ordered team pairs: exploit available 33.3%, trap 23.3%, both 6.7%, neither 50.0%; median best edge 3.79%. The record notes edges depend only on the defense (e.g. DAL PNR +9.2% for every offense), so they are not matchup-specific. Its verdict is descriptive.

ORL-DET opponent-specific decomposition: all top openers were 'universal only' (opponent-specific share +1.4% to +6.9%); DET was within ±5% of league on all seeded play types. No opponent-specific edge was detected in either direction.

2024-25 shot-level PNR share of half-court shots ranged from about 7.6% (OKC) to 13.8% (IND). Possession-level PNR rates were later calibrated to about 17.9–19.6%. The record states there is no pass/fail gate and the rates are a calibration input.

Falsification T3 on the playoff A1 sample: the in-game adapter PPP lift did not carry over to Game N+1 (no PPP lift, negative mix-carry). The record's auto_failure_mechanism is B_powered_null, but its sample_and_power is NOT_RECORDED.

Four playoff games: team-level PNR lifts were small (ORL vs DET PNR +1.2pp; POR vs SAS PNR -4.1pp). Player-channel lifts were large but on n of about 15–54, with helper-steal attribution issues and no holdout.

Raw TOV-force channel lifts shrank by about 50% or more under opponent re-route and counter adjustments (e.g. ORL +8.4pp to net +3.7pp), on 4 games and 8 offense-defense sides. The net lift is model-implied rather than observed in games.

Holdout evaluation on 520 matchup cells and 69,876 possessions: equilibrium R2 -0.1981, actual-mix R2 -0.7167, team-offense mean R2 +0.1197. The lambda sweep worsened R2 monotonically. Predictors built from matchup mixes did not beat simple team means.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Labelling on-ball defensive coverage (DROP/ICE/SWITCH) from NBA matchup and PBP fields
failed_approaches.why: Label rates were very low (14.9% and 3.3%), switches_on was unpopulated, and the record classes the failure as A_unanswerable with LABEL_ERROR and SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER risks.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Play-type inference that used the assisted flag
failed_approaches.why: The assisted flag exists only on makes, which inflated SPOT_UP to 2.83 PPP. The record classes this as C_artifact. Play-type labels built from PBP can carry outcome-derived artifacts.
Cell sizes of about 15–54 were too small, primary-defender attribution included helper steals, and there was no holdout. The record classes this as A_unanswerable with EXPOSURE_SPARSITY.
Lifts shrank by about 50% or more after adjustment, and the net lift was model-implied, not observed. The record's mechanism is E_unclear and the verdict is descriptive.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Matchup-equilibrium and actual-mix predictors of matchup PPP
failed_approaches.why: Both had negative R2 on 520 holdout cells, while the simple team-offense mean scored +0.1197. The record's verdict is tool_eval_fail.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Opponent-specific play-type edge hypothesis for ORL-DET
failed_approaches.why: No opponent-specific edge was detected. Shares were +1.4% to +6.9%, and the record's mechanism is E_unclear.

evidence_establishes: Several earlier studies in this project found that matchup-level or channel-level lifts from play-by-play shrink substantially under adjustment or holdout, and that small cells are unstable.
Play-type labels derived from PBP have a documented artifact history (assisted-flag leak), so PULL_UP and PNR-fail labels need validation before use.
Coverage labels from the matchup feed were sparse, so a conditioning event defined from defensive scheme labels may not be observable at useful rates.
A holdout validation of play-type efficiency ranking (FAM:SF-APPA-063) shows that play-type efficiency is partly predictable at the game-team level, but it does not test counters.
evidence_does_not_establish: No retrieved record tests whether PNR failure is followed by a PULL_UP counter, or measures PULL_UP lift in PNR-fail sequences.
No retrieved record reports the lift distribution across units, the share of units with positive lift, or the median lift against the 2pp threshold.
No retrieved record defines a PNR-fail event or a baseline for PULL_UP outcomes.
Nothing here shows whether 2022-23 through 2025-26 data, including the partial 2025-26 playoffs, would give enough units or possessions for the stated criteria.
The records do not establish the direction or size of any counter effect; the nearest records are descriptive or null.
own_inferences: The question as posed is a conditional with two labels (PNR-fail and PULL_UP) whose definitions are not specified in the question. Each unit needs a fixed baseline and a fixed PULL_UP rate, which the question does not supply.

The 70% and 2pp criteria are unweighted across units, so a few large-volume units could dominate or small units could drive the median. Units of different sizes would not be comparable without an explicit weighting or pooling rule.
PNR-fail sequences are likely rare for any single defensive unit. Lifts in individual units would then rest on few possessions, which the records already flag as a source of unstable estimates.

The nearest prior work (team-level PNR lifts of about +1.2pp and -4.1pp in FAM:SF-APPA-066) suggests 2pp may be a large effect relative to what the data have shown, though the records do not measure this for PULL_UP.
uncertainties: The exact definition of 'units' is not given in the question; the earlier studies used teams, team pairs, or matchup cells.
The definition and frequency of PNR-fail in the play-by-play data are not documented in any retrieved record.
Whether the 2025-26 partial data are included in the test window is not specified.
FAM:SF-CHT-020 has no sample size recorded (sample_and_power NOT_RECORDED), which limits how much weight its null can bear.
Retrieval returned only ten records and was not followed by search_documents or read_family; a more targeted search for prior counter-lift studies could reveal closer prior work.

historical_effect.explanation: The retrieved records do not test the question, but they identify three specific blockers: play-type labels can be artifacts (FAM:SF-PAP-096), coverage-label-based conditioning events are sparse (FAM:SF-APPS-058), and unit-level matchup lifts shrink or fail under holdout (FAM:SF-APPA-067, FAM:SF-APPA-020). Together these moved the decision from proceed toward do_not_proceed for a confirmatory test in its current form.

blocking_constraints.text: The PNR-fail and PULL_UP event rates are not documented, and the 2pp threshold cannot be judged without a stated baseline PULL_UP rate.
Per-unit PNR-fail sequences are likely rare, so counter lift per unit may rest on very few possessions, as in FAM:SF-APPA-066.
PNR-fail and PULL_UP are derived from play-by-play, and FAM:SF-APPS-058 and FAM:SF-PAP-096 show label-coverage and artifact failures.
If PNR-fail is defined by the possession's points, the conditioning event is contaminated by the outcome being tested.
The 70% and median-lift criteria depend on unit definition and weighting, which the question does not fix.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests PNR-fail followed by PULL_UP as a counter or reports the unit-level lift distribution the question asks for. Related earlier work covers play-type efficiency ranking (supported, FAM:SF-APPA-063), opponent-specific edges (FAM:SF-APPA-034 not a hypothesis test; FAM:SF-APPM-012 inconclusive), and matchup-channel lifts that shrink or fail under adjustment (FAM:SF-APPA-067, FAM:SF-APPA-066, FAM:SF-APPA-020). These are adjacent evidence, not an answer.

risks.text: No baseline PULL_UP rate is specified, so a 2pp lift has no reference point; the question's criteria cannot be evaluated as stated.
PNR-fail sequences per unit may be too few for stable per-unit lift, as flagged in FAM:SF-APPA-066.
Per-unit tests across the seasons may be underpowered for a 2pp effect; no power calculation exists.
PNR-fail and PULL_UP labels from play-by-play are unvalidated, and FAM:SF-APPS-058 showed low label coverage.
Without a placebo sequence, any positive lift could reflect general PULL_UP efficiency rather than a counter (as FAM:SF-PAP-096 and FAM:SF-APPA-063 suggest for high-PPP play types).
Shot quality, player quality, and game state are not controlled, and team identity may drive both PNR failure and PULL_UP use.
Testing across many units and play types without correction inflates false positives; FAM:SF-APPA-034 found many units with edges.
PNR-fail defined from points scored would make the outcome part of the conditioning event.
Play-type and PNR rates shift across seasons (FAM:SF-APPM-058, FAM:SF-APPA-063), so pooled estimates may mask trends.
Lifts near zero are expected from regression to the mean when units are selected on extreme prior values.

design.estimand: Average difference in PULL_UP points per possession between PNR-fail sequences and matched non-PNR-fail baselines, within each defensive unit, with the share of units with positive lift and the median lift in pp.
design.unit: Defensive team (30 units) per season, with a secondary team-pair unit if sample sizes allow; PNR-fail possessions per unit must be counted before any test.
design.sample: Regular season 2022-23 to 2024-25 and 2025-26 (complete games only, from 2026-04-13); playoffs as a separate, held-out stratum; exclude partial 2025-26 playoffs.
design.power: Must be computed on a pilot count of PNR-fail possessions per unit before the test. If fewer than about 100 PNR-fail possessions per unit, the per-unit test is not powered for a 2pp effect and the pooled test should be the primary analysis.
design.controls: Match baseline possessions on shot distance, shooter quality, score margin, period, and clock; control for team pace and opponent offensive rating; use a placebo sequence (non-PNR action followed by PULL_UP) as a negative control.
design.falsification: Placebo sequences should show lift of about zero; a counter effect should disappear on the held-out playoff stratum.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register the 70% and 2pp criteria as the single primary test; correct any unit-level or play-type secondary tests with Holm or FDR.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the share of units with positive lift is at least 70% AND the median lift exceeds 2pp, AND the placebo lift is near zero, AND the effect holds on the held-out playoff stratum. Otherwise report as uncertain or rejected.
design.data_version: NBA stats API play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters and box score, 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular season (2025-26 complete only) and 2022-23 to 2024-25 playoffs; derived play-type records from the graph database, with the assisted-flag fix (FAM:SF-PAP-096) and the label-validation step applied first.

What unit definition and minimum sample size are needed to estimate counter lift reliably?
How should possession-level play-type labels derived from play-by-play be validated and protected against outcome-derived labeling?

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

messages.content:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

{"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["PNR fail", "PULL_UP counter", "defensive suppression", "counter strategy effectiveness", "league-wide lift in percentage points", "play type possession records"], "methodological_questions": ["Does conditioning on PNR failure and the subsequent PULL_UP action yield a positive lift across units in at least 70% of units with median lift above 2 percentage points?", "What unit definition and minimum sample size are needed to estimate counter lift reliably?", "How should possession-level play-type labels derived from play-by-play be validated and protected against outcome-derived labeling?"], "query": "PNR fail followed by PULL_UP counter lift league-wide units percentage points defensive suppression"}}

{"results": [{"id": "FAM:SF-APPA-067", "score": 0.793, "document": "# FAM:SF-APPA-067 | Study family SF-APPA-067: TOV_FORCE 3-ply adversarial surviving lift
- observed_research_question: TOV_FORCE 3-ply adversarial surviving lift
- auto_outcome_status: not a hypothesis test
- observed_hypothesis: Raw R1 TOV-force channel lifts survive opponent re-route or PT-shift (R2) and our follow-the-ball counter (R3).
- observed_result: R1 lifts shrink ~50%+: ORL Banchero/Huerter +8.4 to net +3.7pp; DET Green/Anthony +7.0 to +3.5; PHI Harris/Vucevic +12.0 to +6.0; BOS Holiday/Council +6.1 to +2.8; PHX Booker/Wiggins +14.8 to +7.5; OKC Dort/Coffey +12.0  [cut; read_family for the full text]
